newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials seen mixed in coming days.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials seen mixed in coming days.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares traded predictably mixed on Wednesday, with declines leading advances by 16 to nine and brokers expecting little change in coming days on cautious sentiment.
"The outlook is mixed to soft because a lot of investors are trading cautiously as they watch developments around the market," one broker commented.
Share analysts see many local corporate and individual playing the market soft until some new issues are floated on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) in March.

The ZSE's key industrial index recorded its third consecutive fall this week, dropping 11.36 points to 10,593.11 despite some strong and reasonable support in bluechip banking group Barclays, which gained 100 cents to 3,500.
The industrial index was partly driven down by losses in another bluechip, clothing retailer Edgars which traded 200 cents down at 4,700, a day after dropping 100 cents.
Brokers said investor support in minings remained "reasonable", with gold miners Falgold and coal producer Wankie trading 10 and five cents up respectively at 80 and 515.
But 50-cent loss in gold company Rio Tinto at 2,250, left the secondary seven-share mining index 0.08 points down to 957.44.
